item.research_question: How can optimal process parameters be established for in situ alloying of Ti6Al4V with Cu during Laser Powder Bed Fusion to achieve dense parts with required mechanical properties and antibacterial functionality?
item.material_system: Ti6Al4V (ELI) + 1 at % Cu (1.38 wt %) powder mixture
item.processing_route: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) using EOSINT M280 machine; laser power 170 W, spot size 80 µm, layer thickness 30 µm (3D) or 60 µm (tracks/layers), scanning speed 0.7–1.3 m/s, hatch distance 70–100 µm, with single scan and rescan strategies
item.test_conditions: Vickers hardness (200 gf), tensile tests (0.5 mm/min strain rate), SEM-EDS for elemental distribution, EBSD for phase identification, antibacterial testing against E. coli and S. aureus (10^5 CFU/ml, 24 h incubation at 37 °C)
key_findings: Hardness increased from 383 ± 13 HV0.2 (pure LPBF Ti6Al4V) to 456 ± 20 HV0.2 for the Cu-alloyed material.
Ultimate tensile strength increased from 1243 ± 49 MPa (pure) to 1550 ± 126 MPa for the Cu-alloyed material.
Cu concentration at the surface ranged from 1.05 wt % (0.7 m/s, 70 µm hatch) to 2.31 wt % (1.3 m/s, 100 µm hatch) using single scan.
Rescan strategy removed majority of copper segregations and improved surface quality.
In the bulk, Cu content varied: 1–1.5 wt % in α′-martensite regions, 2–5 wt % at pool boundaries, and up to 35 wt % in dendritic/cellular regions.
Dendritic/cellular regions with >30 wt % Cu exhibited a Ti-cubic (β) structure, while 1–5 wt % Cu regions retained α′-hexagonal structure.
Antibacterial testing showed a one-order-of-magnitude decrease in E. coli growth and a two-order-of-magnitude decrease in S. aureus growth.
Crack nucleation at the surface was associated with regions containing 20–35 wt % Cu, likely corresponding to β-Ti cubic structures.
item.mechanism: Segregation of Cu at molten pool boundaries is explained by differences in viscosity and density between molten Cu and Ti6Al4V; Cu has lower viscosity and higher density, causing it to sink and agglomerate near boundaries if convection is insufficient. The formation of β-Ti cubic structure in Cu-rich areas is due to Cu acting as a β-stabilizer alongside V, stabilizing the high-temperature phase down to room temperature under rapid cooling.
item.limitations: Complete alloy homogeneity was not achieved in the bulk; surface roughness influenced tensile test results, making mini-samples behave like notch specimens; diffusion was suppressed due to high cooling rates, potentially leading to higher Cu solubility than equilibrium limits.
item.future_work: Further optimization of manufacturing parameters and heat treatment investigations are required to achieve a homogeneous alloy with tailored mechanical properties; biocompatibility, bioadhesion, and corrosion resistance must be investigated; testing should include emerging pathogens and isolates from failed implants.
quotes: Segregation of Cu at boundaries of the molten pool, and generally observed inhomogeneity of the LPBF manufactured Ti6Al4V (ELI)-1% Cu alloy, could be explained with respect to properties of the feedstock materials.
The presence of Cu in Ti6Al4V alloy discs resulted in a one order of magnitude decrease in the growth of E. coli and notable two order of magnitude decrease in growth of S. aureus.
It could be due to the repeating complete re-melting of the material.
